```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(bibliometrix)
library(ggplot2)
recs <- convert2df("data/wos_export_2024-02.txt", dbsource = "wos", format = "plaintext")
```

# Introduction

The term "citizen science" has spread rapidly through the research
literature since the early 2000s [@bonney2009; @silvertown2009]. This
short analysis describes how fast, in which fields, and where.

We searched the Web of Science Core Collection on 20 February 2024
for records with "citizen science" or "citizen scientist\*" in the
title, abstract or keywords. After removing duplicates and editorials
we retained `r nrow(recs)` records.

# Growth over time

```{r fig-growth, fig.cap="Records per year. The 2023 count may be incomplete.", fig.height=3.5}
yr <- as.data.frame(table(recs$PY))
names(yr) <- c("year", "n")
ggplot(yr, aes(as.integer(as.character(year)), n)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Records (log scale)")
```

Annual output grew roughly exponentially until about 2016 and has
grown more slowly since. Fitting $\log n_t = a + b t$ to the years
2005--2016 gives a doubling time of about
`r round(log(2) / coef(lm(log(n) ~ as.integer(as.character(year)), data = subset(yr, as.integer(as.character(year)) %in% 2005:2016)))[2], 1)`
years.

# Fields

```{python fields}
import pandas as pd
cats = pd.read_csv("data/wos_categories.csv")
top = cats.groupby("category").size().sort_values(ascending=False).head(8)
print(top.to_string())
```

Ecology and environmental sciences together account for about half of
all records. Astronomy, which was prominent in the late 2000s because
of Galaxy Zoo [@lintott2008], is now a much smaller share. The
fastest-growing categories since 2018 are public health and education
research.

| Category                       | Records | Share  |
|:-------------------------------|--------:|-------:|
| Ecology                        |   2,914 |  27.1% |
| Environmental Sciences         |   2,301 |  21.4% |
| Biodiversity Conservation      |   1,187 |  11.0% |
| Multidisciplinary Sciences     |     642 |   6.0% |
| Public, Environmental Health   |     598 |   5.6% |
| Education & Educational Res.   |     411 |   3.8% |

: Top Web of Science categories, 2000--2023.

# Geography

Authors from the United States appear on `r round(100 * mean(grepl("USA", recs$AU_CO)), 0)`%
of records, and from the United Kingdom on about a fifth. Output from
Brazil, China and South Africa has grown fastest in relative terms.
Research on citizen science in Japan (市民科学) uses the term less
often in English-language abstracts, so it is probably undercounted
here [cf. @kobori2016, p. 7].

# Limitations

- Web of Science under-represents non-English and grey literature.
- Many projects that are citizen science in practice use other terms
  ("volunteer monitoring", "community-based monitoring",
  "participatory sensing") and are missed by our query.
- Category assignments are at the journal level.
